newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Demand for dollars from local importers and London banks outweighed selling on Tuesday afternoon, leading the rand weaker at the official close.

At 1420 GMT the local unit was quoted at 4.4830/4860 on the dollar from 4.4680/4750 late on Monday. Against the crosses, it was at 7.0291/0383 on sterling from 6.9701/9801 on Monday and at 0.3308/3313 marks from 0.3322/3328 marks previously.
Dealers said the rand rose due to players being caught short of dollars in the morning.
"We saw a lot of dollar demand from local importers and out of London, driving the rand up to the 4.49 level where exporters started showing interest," a trader said.

"This was again countered by London selling and the rand eventually ended slightly weaker. But we expect a test of 4.47 on Wednesday and there are still a lot of guys out there talking about the 4.45 level," he added.

Although sentiment had been dented by local bond market weakness, in turn triggered by nervousness about U.S. bond yields which rose on the back of the U.S. attack on Iraq early on Tuesday, dealers said the bias was towards more strength.
Events in Iraq had more of a knock on effect on the local bond market than the currency market, they said.

There, local and offshore selling saw yields break the key 15.38 level in the afternoon to an intraday worst of 15.415 percent on the back of lower U.S. Treasuries following the U.S. strike against Iraq.
The August U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management index of manufacturing activity came out in line with expectations, dampening speculation of a tightening of U.S. credit policy.
"We saw a lot of jobbers getting out of long positions as well as re-shuffling of institutional books," a bond trader said.
"Generally, the mood is still postitive but there is caution about the U.S. market which everyone will be watching closely tomorrow (Wednesday)," he added.
Dealers said the two major events of the week to watch out for were local reserves figures and key August U.S. payroll data, both due out on Friday.
At 1420 GMT the R150 was quoted at 15.38 percent from 15.25 percent on Monday, while Eskom's 168 was trading at 15.54 percent from 15.39 previously.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 188.5 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after selling 89.73 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.09 billion rand on Monday after 7.16 billion rand on Friday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were unchanged at between 15.90 to 16.05 percent, while 90-day BAs were also steady at between 15.30 to 15.50 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the money market shortage at 8.141 billion rand on Monday from 8.183 billion rand on Saturday.
